facility_roles.note: H1 was built and operated at DESY on the HERA ring.
The HERA electron/positron and proton beams that H1 recorded were produced and accelerated at DESY.

physics_goals.quote: The main interest of research of the H1 collaboration is to measure the structure of the proton, to study the fundamental interactions between particles, and to search for physics beyond the Standard Model of the elementary particles.
physics_goals.value: Measure the structure of the proton, study the fundamental interactions between particles, and search for physics beyond the Standard Model

summary.plain: A particle detector at the German laboratory DESY, in Hamburg, that watched electrons and protons collide head-on to map out what a proton is made of. It ran from 1992 until HERA, the collider it depended on, shut down in 2007.
summary.technical: General-purpose detector at one of the two collision points of the DESY HERA electron-proton collider (Hamburg, Germany), studying deep inelastic ep scattering to measure proton structure, test QCD and the electroweak theory, and search for physics beyond the Standard Model. Operated May 1992 to June 2007.
